author: Life in the 1800s
description:
I visited the historic 55-acre 18th-century estate and farm known as Locust Grove in Louisville, Kentucky. In this video, I explore the various outbuildings that were essential to farm life, sharing the history and purpose of each one.

Built around 1792 by Major William Croghan, an Irish immigrant who arrived in America as a young man and initially served in the British army before switching sides to join the Patriots at the outbreak of the Revolutionary War. After the war, Croghan married Lucy Clark, sister of the renowned General George Rogers Clark—a Revolutionary War hero famous for his campaigns in the Northwest Territory, including the capture of Vincennes, and credited as the founder of Louisville—who resided at Locust Grove from 1809 to 1818.
title: Walking Through a 200-Year-Old Farm
